market: DiDi Mexico registry expansion — La Paz, Mazatlán, and Acapulco
lane: exact city/BP registry, canonical-brief maturity, current/future corridor evidence, and demand/fare sourcing

existing_atlas_baseline.head: 749b10b7e269000c54ceaf9fbc8feb73e2967da3
existing_atlas_baseline.exact_match_method: Case/accent-insensitive text and structured-ID scan for La Paz, Mazatlán/Mazatlan, Acapulco, Pichilingue, Roqueta, Caleta and Isla de la Piedra; then structured inspection of Mexico cluster cities, route endpoints/IDs and DiDi _map_scope.
existing_atlas_baseline.result: No canonical city IDs, aliases, route IDs, features, BPs or city briefs matched any of the three cities. Mexico cluster currently contains Los Cabos and Puerto Vallarta on the Pacific plus Caribbean cities; DiDi _map_scope includes those existing Mexico IDs, not these three.
existing_atlas_baseline.partner_json_note: Current Mexico-Pacific partner narrative mentions a future longer trunk toward La Paz, but La Paz has no canonical city/BP binding; this is narrative opportunity, not registry proof.

sources.title: Puerto de Pichilingue
sources.publisher: Administración Portuaria Integral de Baja California Sur (APIBCS)
sources.proves: Pichilingue is 17 km from La Paz, has a ferry zone and passenger/ferry ramps, handles regular La Paz–Mazatlán and La Paz–Topolobampo ferries, and publishes 24°16′08″N, 110°19′39″W.

sources.title: Rutas y horarios
sources.proves: Current operator page lists La Paz–Mazatlán and Mazatlán–La Paz. Live page data at access showed La Paz departures Tue/Thu/Sat (boarding 17:30, departure 19:00, arrival 09:00) and Mazatlán departures Wed/Fri/Sun (boarding 14:30, departure 16:00, arrival 08:00). Page does not state an effective date.

sources.title: Tarifas
sources.proves: Current operator tariff table groups both directions of La Paz–Mazatlán and displays MXN 2,150 for an adult passenger. Page does not state fare effective dates or whether fees/promotions alter checkout price.

sources.title: Datos Abiertos — Transbordadores y Embarcaciones de Ruta (2025)
sources.proves: Official monthly XLS files identify the Mazatlán ferry OD labels, operators, arrivals and passenger movements. Summing all 12 files yields La Paz→Mazatlán entries: 42,000 Baja Ferries + 7,714 Transportación Marítima de California; Mazatlán→La Paz exits: 43,786 + 8,758. Files also report Mazatlán–Puerto Bellato entries/exits.

sources.title: Programa Maestro de Desarrollo Portuario de Mazatlán 2025–2030
sources.proves: Official port plan identifies a ferry terminal/breakwater and states the port serves ferry and cruise passengers. It supports facility existence, not a small-craft berth assignment.

sources.title: Baja Ferries terminal contract
sources.proves: Official port contract names the Terminal de Transbordadores de Mazatlán and a passenger waiting-room operating area.

sources.title: Mazatlán registra 100 por ciento de satisfacción turística durante Semana Santa y Pascua 2026
sources.proves: Municipal tourism survey names “Embarcadero a la Isla de la Piedra” as a real strategic visitor point. It does not provide a berth coordinate, route schedule, fare or passenger count.

sources.title: Playas de Mazatlán
sources.proves: Official destination site says Isla de la Piedra is accessible by launch and clarifies it is a peninsula, strengthening the land-crossing/hand-waypoint gate.

sources.title: Tarifas — ASIPONA Acapulco
sources.proves: Official port site provides the Terminal Marítima address on Av. Costera Miguel Alemán in central Acapulco, confirming an existing passenger maritime facility; local Roqueta use is not established.

sources.title: Descubre la mágica Isla de la Roqueta
sources.proves: Official municipal tourism post says boats carrying tourists to Isla de la Roqueta depart from the pier at Playa Caleta. It does not name or locate the island arrival structure, or provide fare/schedule/pax.

sources.title: Acapulco municipal profile
sources.proves: Government profile identifies Isla de la Roqueta as an island around which visitors navigate by boat; useful as destination/POI evidence, not as boarding-facility proof.

sources.title: Puerto de Mazatlán
sources.proves: Official port landing page explicitly presents ferries to La Paz and port infrastructure.

sources.title: Movimiento portuario mensual — Transbordadores y Embarcaciones de Ruta — December 2025
sources.publisher: ASIPONA Mazatlán / Coordinación General de Puertos y Marina Mercante
sources.proves: One of the 12 official monthly worksheets used for the annual sum; documents field layout and December operator/route/direction/passenger records. S8 links all 12 months.

assessment.evidence: Brief is coherent and partner-neutral but frames Mexico as three resort capitals and omits La Paz, Mazatlán and Acapulco.
Strong general case, no sourced local use case for the three registry-gap cities.
Qualitative and Caribbean-heavy; no La Paz–Mazatlán official ferry totals, fares or local-route null discipline.
Mentions a Los Cabos–La Paz Quanta-LR trunk, but lacks endpoints, verified distance and land-crossing hand-waypoint warning.
No exact route IDs exist for audited cities; all proposed route_id values must remain null.
Should distinguish incumbent overnight RoPax from a prospective fast-water product and preserve non-transferability of port totals.
Still needs port-specific ASIPONA/APIBCS permission, berth assignment and local Capitanía review.
Existing coast-wide language is not a city-level operating calendar. No city-specific service seasonality was verified here.
Only two general links in canonical brief. Add official city/port/operator evidence without inserting DiDi framing.
No canonical city briefs found for La Paz, Mazatlán or Acapulco.

recommended_partner_neutral_enhancements: Add concise city-neutral registry entries and city briefs only after canonical IDs and at least one verified BP per city pass geometry review.
Add Pichilingue and Mazatlán ferry-terminal facts, 2025 incumbent ferry passenger observations, and explicit “not transferable 1:1 to Navier” language.
Add Mazatlán–Isla de la Piedra and Caleta–Roqueta as evidence-backed local opportunities with null fares/pax until authoritative data exists.
Add hand-waypoint and range gates for Sea of Cortez/offshore/peninsula routes; do not imply that all Mexico legs fit Pioneer II.
Do not add DiDi operations or app integration language to canonical briefs.

notes: All three cities have exact-city support on official DiDi Mexico pages, so partner framing can say DiDi operates in La Paz, Mazatlán and Acapulco; do not reduce this to country-only support.

La Paz + Mazatlán offer the strongest substantiated intercity story: DiDi first/last mile at both ends of an incumbent passenger ferry OD. Position the ferry counts as market evidence, not capturable Navier volume.

Mazatlán’s Isla de la Piedra and Acapulco’s Caleta–Roqueta are plausible in-app local tourism layers, but remain geometry/economics holds until exact landing points, operators, schedules, fares and pax are verified.
The existing Los Cabos→La Paz expansion concept needs a La Paz canonical city/BP and a hand-routed East Cape alignment; never draw a straight cross-peninsula segment.
No claim should say DiDi controls ferry demand, has port integration, or already provides pier-side dispatch without partner/port evidence.
